title: Parallelizing Tool Execution and LLM Generation for Low-Latency Agent Serving (PASTE)
event_hint: New agent-serving system that overlaps speculative tool execution with LLM generation to hide tool latency on the agent critical path.
problem: LLM-powered agents run a sequential generation-then-tool-execution loop, and today's serving systems serialize it, leaving tool latency fully exposed on the task critical path.
mechanism: PASTE predicts concrete future tool invocations from recurring agent patterns and speculatively executes them while the LLM is still generating; it isolates speculative results until confirmed by the LLM, and jointly schedules tool execution with returning LLM sessions to avoid shifting bottlenecks onto the GPU.

evidence.claim: Average task completion time reduced by 43.5% across deep research, coding, and scientific-agent workloads.
evidence.baseline: today's serving systems that serialize the generation-execution loop
evidence.condition: deep research, coding, and scientific-agent workloads
speculative tool execution overlapped with LLM generation

evaluation_context: Three agent workload categories: deep research, coding, and scientific agents. Comparison is against conventional serving systems that serialize the model-generation and tool-execution loop.
limitations: Abstract-level only; full body not fetched. Gains depend on recurring/predictable agent tool patterns; the accuracy of the invocation predictor and mis-speculation costs are not quantified in the abstract. Baselines are described generically as 'today's serving systems' without a named system.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent acceleration: it parallelizes speculative tool calls with LLM generation, a scheduling/overlap technique that complements code-graph and parallel-speculative tooling themes. The joint scheduling of tool execution and returning LLM sessions also intersects with GPU-side inference-network/TPN concerns about where bottlenecks move when one stage is parallelized.
